challenge.method: Distinguish language from application classes, hardware and system in the manual’s own terminology. Compare Kay’s participant chronology and the Blue Book’s separate language and implementation treatment.
challenge.results: The preface directly names the Smalltalk language and says it was designed and implemented by people at PARC. Its hardware and surrounding system have separate descriptions. The canonical name and language classification fit this bounded identity. Active denotes the index state.

limitations: The record identifies the programming language at the historical PARC scope.
The source discusses the system running the language and the Interim Dynabook hardware separately. Current implementations and broad classifier aliases are outside its authority.
The exact edition and claim locator were reviewed from the registered publication.
